extracted.intended_audience: prospective MFA students, arts educators, and general readers interested in graduate fine arts degrees
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the typical requirements, structure, and role of the Master of Fine Arts (MFA) degree, including admissions practices, program length and format, culminating requirements, and how the MFA compares with related degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate for an MFA typically holds a bachelor's degree prior to admission; admissions requirements often consist of a sample portfolio of artworks or a performance audition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many institutions do not require that the candidate's undergraduate major conform with their proposed path of study in the MFA program; admissions commonly emphasize demonstrated artistic work (portfolio or audition) over specific prior major.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate major flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Undergraduate major need not match MFA field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions often accept applicants from varied undergraduate backgrounds; suitability is usually judged via artistic sample (portfolio/audition) rather than prior major coursework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program duration
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA typically requires two to three years of postgraduate study after a bachelor's degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term of study varies by country or university; durations cited are typical but not universal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coursework nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Coursework is primarily of an applied or performing nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MFA programs center on professional artistic practice rather than purely academic study, so classes and training emphasize studio work, performance, or practice-based instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culminating requirement (thesis/exhibition/performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program often culminates in a thesis exhibition or performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The capstone is practice-focused (exhibition, recital, performance, screening, etc.), reflecting the applied/professional orientation of the degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplines included
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA covers fine arts fields including visual arts, creative writing, graphic design, photography, filmmaking, dance, theatre, other performing arts, and in some cases theatre management or arts administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MFA programs are offered across many creative disciplines; specific program names and emphases vary by institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from Master of Arts (MA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA differs from the MA in that the MFA centers on professional artistic practice in the particular field, whereas MA programs usually center on the scholarly, academic, or critical study of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction implies different curricular emphases: practice/studio/performance for MFA vs research/critical/theoretical work for MA; it affects career preparation and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal degree recognition (United States)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the United States, an MFA is typically recognized as a terminal degree for practitioners of visual art, design, dance, photography, theatre, film/video, new media, and creative writing—qualifying an individual to become a professor at the university level in these disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition as a terminal degree means the MFA is considered the highest professional degree in those practice-based fields; institutional hiring norms and requirements may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional/organizational standards and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist standards and guidelines documents for MFA programs published by professional organizations (examples cited: College Art Association (CAA) MFA Standards, Association of Writers & Writing Programs (AWP) Hallmarks of a Successful MFA Program, NASAD/NASD/NAST co-published policies, UFVA guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These referenced documents provide more detailed program standards, recommended practices, and evaluative questions for MFA programs across disciplines; the Wikipedia article cites them as authoritative sources though it does not reproduce their full content.
